name: Todai-ji Temple (Eastern Great Temple)
description: Monumental Buddhist temple housing the Daibutsu (15-meter bronze Great Buddha), one of the world's largest wooden buildings.
history: Constructed by Emperor Shomu to bring national unity, peace, and spiritual protection to Japan after epidemics and rebellions.
construction: Built from massive ancient cedar pillars and bronze casting using an estimated 500 tonnes of copper, tin, and gold leaf.
architecture: Massive hip-and-gable roof structure with double eaves and dramatic golden Shibi roof ridge ornaments.
significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site as part of the Historic Monuments of Ancient Nara.
currentStatus: Active temple and national treasure in Nara, Japan.
